title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 177
paragraphs: These places, then, the Greeks perceived to be suited to their purpose; for they considered everything carefully beforehand and calculated that the barbarians would not be able to take advantage either of their superior numbers or of their cavalry. They therefore resolved to receive the invader of Greece here. When they were informed that the Persian was in Pieria, they broke up from the Isthmus and set out on campaign, some going by land to Thermopylae, others making for Artemisium by sea.
